tells.1: Stripped-down, uniform declarative sentences ('Stepwise is for...', 'Stepwise is free to download') that read like a mechanical de-fluffing pass rather than marketing copy
tells.2: none (only human quirks: the clichéd 'Never miss a session again', the exclamation point, and the boilerplate '24-hours prior' phrasing)
tells.3: Specifics that look invented and can't be verified: a testimonial from 'Gwen Harper', an exact '312' exercise count, a Premium feature claim, and an 'In our experience... more than...' contrast framing
tells.4: Generic filler phrasing ('guidance you can trust', 'keep your recovery moving', 'unlock more of what the app has to offer') plus neatly parallel bolded benefit leads
tells.5: A slightly over-smoothed conversational tone ('Maybe you're bouncing back...', 'keep you moving forward'), though it reads naturally

reason: Version 2 has the uneven, slightly clunky feel of real human-written store copy. Version 5 keeps that natural voice but is clearer and more polished, and unlike Version 3 it makes no unverifiable claims, so it's the safest and strongest one to publish.
